I5.quote: Orange peels and tea leaves accumulate as everyday “breakfast bio-waste” all around the world.

notes: KOH-activated carbons from used tea leaves and orange peels; H2 measured volumetrically at 77 K, 0-1 bar (Autosorb iQ3) and 0-100 bar (PCTPro-2000 manometric, excess). BET areas for all eight samples (Table 3). Paper defines its excess wt% as m(H2)/(m(s)+m(H2)), i.e. W2 (p. 522, Section 2.3). Three additional samples in the Kendall analysis and Table 6 come from the group's earlier papers [4,5,16,28], but the eight UTL/OP samples are presented as new; no statement that all uptake values were published before, so duplicate_data does not apply. Not a review; record and PDF give no retraction.
